common_name: Apollo Pepper (PuckerButt Carolina Reaper x Pepper X Superhot Cross)

planting.note: Start seed indoors on a heat mat 10-12 weeks before the last frost, since this chinense superhot is slow to germinate and needs a long, warm season to fruit before cool weather sets in.

directions: Apollo is a Smokin' Ed Currie (PuckerButt Pepper Company) creation that pairs two of his own extreme chilies, Carolina Reaper and Pepper X, into a single superhot line said by the breeder and pepper enthusiasts to push past 3 million Scoville units, among the hottest named peppers ever reported. It is grown and sold mostly in small quantities for collectors rather than as a mainstream garden variety, and its wrinkled, rounded pods resemble a Carolina Reaper, sometimes with a short tail. Expect a fruity, earthy flavor buried deep beneath an intense, lingering burn, and always wear gloves when handling or harvesting ripe fruit. Give plants a long warm season, full sun, and stake them once pods set, since fruit load can be heavy for the plant's size.

common_name: Death Spiral Pepper (UK Naga Bubblegum x Naga Viper Superhot Cross)

planting.note: Start seed indoors on a heat mat 8-10 weeks before the last frost; this UK-bred hybrid is a slow, vigorous grower that needs a full warm season to ripen a heavy crop.

directions: Death Spiral is a British hybrid of Naga Bubblegum and Naga Viper best known for its gnarled, twisted, brain-like pods that often taper into a pronounced stinger tail. Color runs from green through peach and orange before settling on red, and individual fruit frequently stalls at an intermediate shade rather than coloring up fully. Heat sits around 1,400,000 Scoville units, roughly matching the lower end of Carolina Reaper, yet a surprising fruity sweetness with citrus and floral notes still comes through beneath the burn. It is a specialty, collector-grown variety rather than a supermarket type, so source seed from dedicated superhot seed vendors and reserve the harvest for extreme hot sauces.

common_name: Apocalypse Scorpion Pepper (Italian AIASP Superhot Scorpion-Type)

planting.note: Start seed indoors on a heat mat 8-10 weeks before the last frost; as an unstabilized hybrid, plants and fruit can vary somewhat from seed to seed.

directions: Apocalypse Scorpion was developed by members of AIASP, an Italian association of chile growers known for hybridizing extreme-heat peppers, and carries heat of 1,400,000 Scoville units or more, rivaling Carolina Reaper. Pods run 2-3 inches long with warped, pock-marked skin and the classic scorpion stinger tail, ripening from green to red. Despite the ferocity of the burn, which builds gradually and lingers for ten minutes or longer, tasters report sweet, fruity, and unusually floral notes up front. Because it remains an unstandardized hobbyist cross, grow it from specialty superhot seed and use only slivers of the ripe fruit in sauces, chilis, or stews.

common_name: Kraken Scorpion Pepper (Bhut Jolokia India Carbon x Trinidad Scorpion Chocolate Cross)

planting.note: Start seed indoors on a heat mat 8-10 weeks before the last frost, and plan for a tall, sprawling plant that will need staking once pods load up.

directions: Mike Hess of Peoria, Illinois bred Kraken Scorpion in 2013 by crossing Bhut Jolokia India Carbon with Trinidad Scorpion Chocolate, producing a large, dark brown, elongated pod 3-4 inches long with rough, pimply skin and occasionally a short tail. Heat runs 1,000,000 to 1,200,000 Scoville units, and the flavor opens floral, earthy, and faintly smoky before a delayed, lingering burn takes over. Plants grow unusually tall for a chinense superhot, often topping four feet, and reward staking and a long warm season with a heavy harvest. Reserve the fruit for extreme hot sauces, barbecue sauce, or dried chile flakes where its smoky-floral character stands out.

common_name: Black Scorpion Tongue Pepper (Purple-to-Red Ornamental Hot Pepper)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; this compact variety does double duty as a bedding or container plant as well as a culinary chile.

directions: Black Scorpion Tongue is an American-bred ornamental annuum valued for pods that emerge nearly black-purple and ripen through red, sometimes developing dark striping or blotches where sun exposure is most intense, so a single plant can show several pod colors at once. Fruit is small, 1-2 inches long and about three-quarters of an inch wide, with a crisp, crunchy texture and a sweet, fruity, floral flavor with hints of apple that mellows as pods redden. Heat is moderate for a specialty pepper, in the 50,000-100,000 Scoville range, well short of true superhot territory but still a solid step above a jalapeño. The tall, heavily fruiting plants make a dramatic landscaping accent while still supplying usable pods for hot sauces, infused oils, and fresh salsas.
